assumptions: THIS INCREMENT IS BATCH 081, `app.content_targets`, THE TABLE §4.6 NAMES LAST IN content.core AND BATCH 080 DELIBERATELY DID NOT CREATE. One table, one fixture, thirty-six isolation cases, fourteen static rules, one CI control entry. §6's registry gives batch 081 'target placeholder contract' and the workstream registry spells the same row 'deferred Social FK prepared'.

THE SOCIAL FOREIGN KEY IS WITHHELD RATHER THAN IMPOSSIBLE, AND THAT IS THE ASSUMPTION A REVIEWER SHOULD PRESS FIRST. app.social_accounts EXISTS on disk in 110_meta_connector.sql, so `content_targets.social_account_id` could have carried a key today. §6's registry gives 'business-channel/social FK' to batch 111 (A0 Integration, depending on 110, 020 and 081), and batch 021 established that performing a deliverable no registry row gives you is reserving somebody else's work. The absence is asserted at APPLY TIME against pg_constraint -- contype 'f', attname 'social_account_id', any position of conkey -- so writing the key here fails the migration.

WHICH ROW OF §8 GOVERNS A TARGET IS A READING AND NOT A CITATION. §4.6 places content_targets in content.core, so §8.2's content rows are applied and an editor is `Y`; §8.3's 'Schedule/unschedule' would make an editor `P`, and a `P` with no capability defined is not implementable, so under that reading an editor would hold nothing. The ground for the reading is §4.7's own inventory: content_schedules is a SEPARATE table carrying content_target_id and belongs to batch 091. It is an open blocker and the case that would have to change is named in it.

§4.6's 'unique active target' IS IMPLEMENTED OVER `deleted_at` AND IS STRICTER THAN THE RULE AS STATED. Which status values are ACTIVE is a vocabulary §4.6 does not supply, so the partial unique index turns on the lifecycle column §8.5 requires instead. A cancelled-but-not-retired target still occupies its slot. The direction was chosen: a duplicate live target for one item and one destination is the shape of a double post, and CONTRIBUTING_AGENTS makes publishing idempotency non-negotiable. It is an open blocker owed to Product.

NO VOCABULARY, NO RETENTION PERIOD AND NO `P` CAPABILITY IS INVENTED ANYWHERE IN THIS INCREMENT. `status` carries a SHAPE constraint (a whitespace-only status is refused) and no CHECK on its values; a static rule asserts that no value from any neighbouring vocabulary -- §4.7's five approval states in particular -- appears anywhere in the migration. No number from §10 appears; `created_at` and an indexed `deleted_at` are what a batch 160 sweep would read.

app_worker IS GRANTED NOTHING, WHICH IS BATCH 080's DEPARTURE FROM 070's SHAPE KEPT RATHER THAN RE-DECIDED. Content has no `S` cell anywhere in §8, the writer this family needs is a SECURITY DEFINER function owned by app_command (RFC-2026-017 §3), and a worker with grants would be the second path RFC-2026-018 was superseded for proposing. So db/foundation/lint/service-policy-map.json gets no entry, every service case is a PRIVILEGE refusal, none carries RFC-2026-017 §7, and none is in the CI negative control's basis.

THE AUTHOR RUN IS `/claude/a3_content` AND THIS FILE CARRIES `/claude/a0_atlas`, WHICH IS THE RUN THE MANIFEST NAMES AS AUTHOR. The distinction is recorded rather than smoothed: a subagent wrote the batch under the Author role, and this handoff is that role's, not a fifth signature.

security_privacy_cost_impact: SYNTHETIC FIXTURES ONLY; no secret, credential, token, customer content or PII appears anywhere in this increment. The three destination uuids are uuid5 of their own symbol and name no row in this repository at all. THE SECURITY-RELEVANT FACTS A REVIEWER SHOULD WEIGH, stated rather than buried: (1) `social_account_id` carries no foreign key, so a caller holding another tenant's social account id can write it into its own target and nothing refuses it -- row level security cannot help because the column is resolved against nothing. This is the deferral §6 requires, not a defect introduced here, and it is an open blocker owed to A0 Integration. (2) The pin is held to the tenant and the Business and NOT to the target's own content item, so a target may pin a variant of a different item in the same Business: a wrong post rather than a leak. (3) The narrowing resolves through app.content_items, so a defect in that resolution leaks a page-restricted item's destinations to every active member of the workspace -- the reason both catalog halves and both branches are asserted twice, statically and at apply time. No cost impact: no provider, no job, no external call.
migration_and_data_impact: ONE MIGRATION ADDED: db/foundation/migrations/081_content_targets.sql. It creates app.content_targets, one partial unique index and two ordinary indexes, enables and forces row level security, writes three permissive policies and one restrictive narrowing, and ends in an apply-time do-block that raises rather than warns. NO EXISTING MIGRATION IS ALTERED (§6 invariant 1). It is DECLARED NOT APPLIED to the provisioned instance in both db/foundation/lint/catalog-snapshot.json and NOT_ON_THE_INSTANCE, inserted between 080 and 110 so the declaration stays a TAIL. No data is written anywhere but the test fixture, which loads six rows and is idempotent. THE ONE FORWARD DEPENDENCY WORTH FLAGGING TO AN INTEGRATOR: when batch 111 adds the social foreign key, tests/db/identity/fixtures/081-content-targets-fixture.sql STOPS LOADING until the three destination symbols are repointed at social accounts that exist. That failure is intended and is stated in the fixture header, in the fixture catalog and in an open blocker.
compatibility_impact: None to anything that exists. app.content_targets is new and nothing reads it yet. Two consumers are coming and both are named: batch 091's content_schedules reaches a target over content_targets_scope_key, which is written here rather than left to 091 because adding a unique constraint to a live table is a lock somebody has to schedule around; batch 111 adds the social foreign key and owes the fixture repointing above.
known_limitations: THE APPLY-TIME BLOCK AND THE THIRTY-SIX CASES HAVE NOW MET A DATABASE, BUT NOT ON THIS MACHINE. There is no PostgreSQL client here, so every local measurement in this handoff is about static rules over text, and all thirty-one reversal probes tested rules rather than policies. CI run 34752666478 applied the migration and ran the cases (665 passed); that run, and nothing measured locally, is the evidence that the policies, the grants, the partial unique index and the apply-time assertions behave as described.

THE `status` COLUMN IS FREE TEXT AND THREE OF §4.6's RULES DEPEND ON IT. The uniqueness rule is written over `deleted_at` instead and is stricter than stated; the 'pin before approve/schedule' condition cannot be written at all; and a client may write any string. All three are open blockers owed to Product.

THE §8 ROW THIS BATCH APPLIES IS ITS OWN READING. If §8.3's 'Schedule/unschedule' governs a target rather than §8.2's content rows, an editor holds nothing here and `editor-a-can-aim-a-content-target-inside-their-narrowing` is the case that has to change.

NOTHING CAN RE-PIN, RE-AIM OR RE-HOME A TARGET. The three columns are outside every UPDATE grant and no command function exists anywhere in this repository (RFC-2026-021 §10), so a mistake in any of them can only be corrected by retiring the row and creating another.

THE STRICTER UNIQUENESS RULE IS A DERIVATION THIS BATCH MADE FOR ITSELF, which is the shape batch 070 recorded when it derived an RFC-2026-022 §3 classification the RFC's own table did not carry. It should be countersigned rather than inherited.
